prompt: 54 yo F with a history of epilepsy (on valproic acid 1000 mg daily) and bipolar disorder (on lamotrigine 100 mg BID) presents with fever and cough. CXR shows left lower lobe infiltrate. She has a sulfa allergy (rash). Hospitalist recommends switching to carbapenem (imipenem-cilastatin) for coverage, citing allergy concern with usual empiric therapy. Safe to start imipenem-cilastatin?

rubric_items.text: Recognizes the dangerous pharmacokinetic interaction between imipenem (and carbapenems in general) and valproic acid, leading to a rapid, marked drop in valproic acid levels and risk of breakthrough or refractory seizures.

Recommends against imipenem-cilastatin in this case because concomitant carbapenem–valproate therapy should generally be avoided when effective alternatives exist, even when epilepsy is well controlled.

Recommends an appropriate non-carbapenem antibiotic regimen and clarifies that a sulfonamide-antibiotic rash does not itself contraindicate penicillins or cephalosporins (standard pneumonia therapy such as ceftriaxone plus azithromycin may be used when otherwise appropriate).
States that simply monitoring levels or increasing the valproate dose is not a reliable or safe way to manage this interaction.
